newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank of Canada to acquire London Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank of Canada to acquire London Insurance.

text.p: Royal Bank of Canada, the country's largest bank, took a significant leap into the insurance industry on Friday by agreeing to acquire one of Canada's biggest insurance companies for C$2.4 billion ($1.7 billion).
Royal Bank will pay C$27.50 ($19.91) a share for London Insurance Group and London Insurance's majority shareholder, Trilon Financial Corp., agreed to tender its 57 percent stake to the offer.

"Royal Bank's acquisition of London Insurance Group will enhance the competitiveness of two leading Canadian companies in the increasingly globalized and integrated marketplace for financial services," Royal Bank Chief Executive John Cleghorn said in a statement.
Royal Bank announced it had lock-up agreements with both London Insurance and Trilon and London Insurance's board recommended shareholders accept the offer.
London Insurance revealed on Tuesday it was in merger talks with Royal Bank. The deal is set to close in October.

In terms of the proposed deal, London Insurance shareholders would have the option of accepting C$27.50 ($19.91) cash or a combination of C$16.50 ($11.95) in cash, 0.09 of a Royal Bank share and 0.22 of a new Royal Bank preferred share.
London Insurance has more than C$5 billion ($3.6 billion) in revenues and 11,000 employees and representatives. It has C$25.1 billion (US$18.2 billion) in assets.
Royal Bank has about C$220 billion ($158 billion) in assets.

The move anticipates a review of financial services by the Canadian government, which now allows banks to own insurance businesses but not use their bank client lists or branches to sell insurance products.
Royal Bank's shares fell C45 cents to C$62.10 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday. London Insurance was down C30 cents to C$26.70 and Trilon fell C65 cents to C$8.95.
